name: duet
description: Delegates subagents to Codex: Codex roles Claude can pick (advisor, reviewer, implementer) plus chosen subagent types, in the background or waited on, with independent Codex reviews; measures every run

codexAgents.title: Subagent types sent to Codex
codexAgents.description: Comma-separated subagent types Codex runs instead of Claude, e.g. general-purpose, code-explorer. * sends every type. Named, isolated and nested calls stay on Claude. Empty: only the duet: roles go to Codex.

codexSandbox.title: Codex sandbox
codexSandbox.description: read-only: Codex reads and answers but writes nothing. workspace-write: Codex may also write in the session folder and /tmp. In both, Codex can read any file your account can read. A custom agent whose tools cannot edit always runs read-only.

codexModel.title: Codex model
codexModel.description: Passed to codex as -m. Empty: Codex's own configured model.

maxConcurrent.title: Codex runs at once
maxConcurrent.description: A routed call beyond this many live Codex runs is refused with a reason.

timeoutMinutes.title: Codex timeout (minutes)
timeoutMinutes.description: A Codex run past this is stopped and the call refused. If duet has to fall back to a one-shot run (streaming couldn't start), that run stops at 10 minutes at most.

codexConsent.title: Sending repo content to Codex
codexConsent.description: ask: once per session before the first handoff. allow: pre-approved (needed for headless claude -p).

codexRunMode.title: Wait or background
codexRunMode.description: wait or background for codexAgents types, then overrides by type: advisor=background, Explore=wait. Roles default to advisor wait, reviewer background. A run that can edit always waits.

codexFsScope.title: Codex filesystem scope
codexFsScope.description: anything: Codex's own sandbox, which reads any file your account can read. project: a duet permission profile limits Codex to the session folder (writable only under workspace-write), plus read-only system paths and Codex's own install and memories folders, plus git's own folders in a linked worktree, and hides every other file and, on Linux, /tmp (on macOS, Codex's source makes /tmp readable and writable, even under read-only; not run). On Codex 0.162.1 (Linux), codex exec runs confirmed the hidden files and /tmp; the write limits are partly checked in codex sandbox only (SPEC, Change 0.2.6). Re-check after upgrading Codex.

codexWritePaths.title: Folders an agent may write
codexWritePaths.description: With codexFsScope project and workspace-write: agent=folder;folder entries, comma-separated, e.g. red-test-writer=tests;test. A named agent writes only those project folders and reads the rest; others write the whole project. A folder outside the project or in .git, .codex or .agents (also through a symlink), or not there yet, is ignored and named in the run's result; a malformed value leaves every agent read-only.

apiCustomUrl.title: Custom provider base URL
apiCustomUrl.description: The custom API provider's OpenAI-compatible base URL (https://, or http:// to localhost), e.g. https://my-gateway.example.com/v1 for Azure OpenAI, LiteLLM, LM Studio or a company gateway. Its key is DUET_CUSTOM_API_KEY, entered in /duet provider.

apiCustomModel.title: Custom provider default model
apiCustomModel.description: The model id that runs on the custom provider will use (0.4.0). For now the key test lists the models instead, and /duet provider test custom <model> names one directly.
